head.title: Importing and debugging in Visual Studio Code IDE

section.name: Import
section.p:
Before importing the project into Visual Studio Code, install the
Extension Pack for Java from the Visual Studio Code Marketplace.

Open Visual Studio Code and select File -> Open Folder..., then choose the cloned checkstyle repository root directory containing pom.xml. Visual Studio Code will automatically detect the Maven project and import all dependencies.

img.alt: Import Checkstyle project in Visual Studio Code

section.name: Debug
section.p:
Open a Check's source file or unit test file in the Explorer sidebar.
Set a breakpoint by clicking to the left of the line number in the editor gutter.
Open the corresponding unit test file (for example, in src/test/java), right-click the test method or click the Debug Test lens above the method to start debugging.
Use the Debug toolbar to control execution: Continue (F5), Step Over (F10), Step Into (F11), and Step Out (Shift+F11).

section.name: Organize Imports
section.p: One of the Checkstyle checks we run on our own code requires a specific order of import statements. You can configure Visual Studio Code's Java settings so that Organize Imports follows Checkstyle's import order automatically.

Open Settings (Ctrl+, or Cmd+, on macOS), search for java.completion.importOrder, and configure the order groups to match Checkstyle's configuration (static imports first, followed by standard Java and third-party packages). You can then format imports in any file using Shift+Alt+O (Shift+Option+O on macOS).
